criteria.title: Planning and milestone authority
criteria.explanation: The core requires retained planning, current specification validation and applicable authority. Acceptance, merge and completion add their respective evidence and action requirements. Failed proof leaves corrective work available.

criteria.title: Model-led execution
criteria.explanation: Readiness records intent without launching evaluation. Execution selects gates explicitly, retains genuine consumed-evidence requirements and imposes no remediation-round limit or general scheduling graph.

criteria.title: Canonical layouts
criteria.explanation: The trusted resolver and local store support repository-local records and shared parent records independently of record Git ownership. Layout fixtures cover untracked, tracked and ignored records without evidence commits.

criteria.title: Exact source and requirements
criteria.explanation: Candidates retain exact requirement bytes, approval references, repository identities, source endpoints, criteria and scope. Preparation and admission reject source drift, foreign identity, incorrect repository roots and incomplete whole-feature rubric coverage.

criteria.title: Containment and isolation
criteria.explanation: Canonical capture rejects traversal, unsafe ancestors and symlink substitution. Reviewer exports contain selected repositories, separately retained requirements and permitted evidence; reserved history is filtered at source endpoints. Provider requests use fresh contexts and read-only, network-denied policies.

criteria.title: Publication and retention
criteria.explanation: Exclusive publication rejects conflicting content; typed closure checks reject missing or altered referenced evidence. Journal witnesses, durable outcome markers and operation identities support interrupted-operation reconciliation. Retention preserves failures and makes no backup claim; workspace deletion requires a scoped retention decision.

criteria.title: Local finalization
criteria.explanation: Packet inventories and retention derive from validated core references. Application cleanliness, reviewed content and PR synchronization remain separate checks; caller path lists and evidence commits cannot substitute for proof.

criteria.title: Independent grouped verdicts
criteria.explanation: Grouped code/spec execution produces separately validated gate results. Missing verdicts, inherited contexts and mismatched receipt bindings cannot qualify. Formal Verification reports an actual fresh evaluator transport round trip and explicitly distinguishes it from this feature's quality verdict.

criteria.title: Complete obligation inventory
criteria.explanation: The current gate inventory preserves every C1 obligation, including separate code, spec and Judge assessments, policy-controlled whiteboard, and completion obligations. Mechanical PASS requires actual successful receipts for every declared check.

criteria.title: Equivalent-input reuse
criteria.explanation: Applicability uses relevant retained content rather than commit or attempt identity alone. Reuse returns original result references and preserves execution provenance while checking configuration, consumed evidence and qualification.

criteria.title: Relevant change and uncertainty
criteria.explanation: Admission rechecks requirements, support documents, helper/interpreter bindings, runtime dependencies, inherited environment, consumed proof and explicit external validity. Runner scope declarations are mandatory; unsupported dependency resolution fails closed.

criteria.title: Targeted delta coverage
criteria.explanation: Delta execution requires qualifying prior proof, unchanged requirement scope, explicit changed-path coverage and assessed interactions. Base, head and target changes participate in coverage; incomplete or unsupported PASS claims are rejected.

criteria.title: Bounded history and dispositions
criteria.explanation: Packets distinguish implementer claims from reviewer conclusions and retain findings, limits and provenance. Open and claimed findings require dispositions; affected closures require independent assessment, while equivalent unaffected closures can carry forward without repetitive enumeration.

criteria.title: New discovery and blocking criteria
criteria.explanation: Evaluator instructions require new defect discovery, including new instances of resolved classes. Blocking findings must cite selected approved criteria or the applicable gate rule and identify current scoped source; unsupported advice does not automatically block.

criteria.title: One scoped human decision
criteria.explanation: One decision can apply named exceptions or amendments and explicitly included continuation actions. Pending records preserve interrupted instructions without granting authority; retries reconcile the same request. Amendments retain previous and new commitments.

criteria.title: Honest exceptions and integration
criteria.explanation: Exceptions remain separate from FAIL/UNAVAILABLE outcomes and bind candidate and risk scope, including transitive consumed evidence. Merge authority must name the prepared action. Actual integration is independently observed rather than inferred from acceptance or a waiver.

criteria.title: Enforcement coverage
criteria.explanation: Protected adapters consult the current core, bind authority to the action and candidate, and reject drift. Native hook manifests route recognized direct merges to a deny-and-route handler. Coverage accurately distinguishes adapter enforcement, tested handler behavior, unverified host interception and cooperative arbitrary-shell behavior.

criteria.title: Coherent consumers and low ceremony
criteria.explanation: CLI, native adapter and desktop consume the same current core. Desktop presents obligations and exceptions without an ordering editor or evaluator launcher. Operations generate requests and receipts; CLI configuration supports explicit runner scope and rejects the retired shortcut.
